_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.stdio.semio.text` is a semio-NATIVE format, so the reference is not a third-party library but a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language — see the oracle entry's rationale.

oracles.rationale: 🐍️ No third party reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so this subset's reference is a SECOND IMPLEMENTATION rather than a third-party distribution — which is why `package` is empty: the entry links no external library and therefore contributes nothing to the dependency ratchet. The implementation is `../../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-semio-text/🐍️component.py`: the semio text envelope, the `stdio.semio.text.snapshot` DSL grammar, the `s.stdio.semio.text.snapshot` pack frame and all seven verbs of the `stdio.semio.text.mutations` grammar, written in Python from those committed specification documents alone. It imports nothing from the Rust it judges and transliterates none of it, so agreement between the two is real evidence: two implementations in two languages, written from one written specification, reaching the same bytes and the same snapshots. Its own reading of the specification is pinned by the fact that it reproduces both committed example artifacts byte for byte and reaches all seven committed handcrafted `(before, mutation, after)` vectors — if it had misread the grammar it could do neither.
